analysis:
The changes in this batch are documentation only. docs/provider/cli-reference.md changes its last-updated date and adds a description of the `status` line "Requests served since the daemon started". docs/provider/troubleshooting.md changes its date, clarifies the `usage reporting` doctor check, and adds a row explaining why `status` can show more requests than console Earnings. I examined the supplied head text of cli-reference.md (lines 1298-1986) and the troubleshooting.md patch. The added-line hunk of cli-reference.md (~990-1001) is only visible in the file_changes patch excerpt, which is complete. None of the supplied text shows executable code, protocol, key-handling, attestation, authorization, or encryption changes, so I see no regression against the canonical threat model.

The new text documents that the served-request counter is local, includes cancelled or dropped requests, and includes free self-route traffic. The counter is explicitly not a payment or earnings record. That framing sets honest expectations and does not overclaim trust. It says nothing that relaxes the position that providers are adversarial. The surrounding cache and prefix-cache documentation (T-041 posture, SSD TTL, DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE gating) appears unchanged in this PR. The new status counter text introduces no extra data exposure beyond aggregate counts, with no prompt content or identifiers.

Remaining integration questions, which are not security regressions: the documented behavior depends on `StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift` and the platform's `coordinator/registry/heartbeat.go` (`cumulativeDelta`), which are not in the supplied evidence. This batch cannot verify that the docs match them. A reviewer who sees those code changes elsewhere in the PR should confirm the counter exposes no sensitive data and is not used as a billing or authorization input.
